attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Doomed' is firm language predicting the strategy will fail. The preceding paragraph defines the mission, and the drafter keeps that scope. No deadline is given.

contract.note: Reading 'failure' as documented collapse or abandonment across a material part of the buildout is fair and ordinary. It sensibly excludes routine refinancing and temporary slowdowns. The result depends on this reading of failure, since the speaker gave no threshold.

evidence.note: Anthropic S-1 dated 2026-10-26. It discloses dependence on capital and partner credit support. That shows financing risk, not that the strategy has failed or become self-financing.
Reuters, 2026-10-19: both labs were still raising money successfully. This weighs against failure so far but does not show lasting self-financing.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet shows neither a documented collapse or abandonment nor a completed self-financing cycle, so the early-resolution rule is not met in either direction. Raising money and disclosing financing risk do not settle it.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A compound present-tense observation: big losses, deep unprofitability, and no answer on how to function without outside support. The last part is partly evaluative and hard to test.

contract.note: Using calendar 2025 net losses and a combined threshold of at least $20B is a reasonable plain reading. It is still the evaluator's choice. The 'no credible route' test asks for proof of a negative and depends on judgment.

evidence.note: Partial support only. OpenAI's audited 2025 net loss was nearly $39B, about $30B of it a one-off charge, which alone clears the combined threshold. It says nothing about Anthropic's losses or either lab's operating plans.

reviews.rationale: The packet supports the scale of OpenAI's loss only. Anthropic's 2025 loss status is not shown in this packet, and nothing tests the claim that neither lab has a credible route to running without outside support. The compound claim cannot be settled on this packet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The drafter rightly drops the 'every publication' line as rhetoric. The proposition keeps both parts: the labs buoy cloud revenue, and the labs cannot exist without tens of billions of outside funding a year.

contract.note: Reading 'buoyed' as a material contribution and using Q2 2026 is fair. But 'buoyed' has no threshold, for example whether ~6% of AWS counts, and the funding-necessity test depends on how cash needs are judged. So interpretation does affect the result, contrary to the contract's flag.

evidence.note: Jefferies estimates for Q2, via secondary reporting: the labs were about 45% of Google Cloud Platform revenue, 25% of Azure and 6% of AWS. That supports a material contribution to revenue. It is silent on the funding requirement.

Anthropic's S-1 shows large GAAP net losses, mostly fair-value charges, alongside positive operating cash flow in H1 2026. This cuts against an annual funding need of tens of billions but does not settle it, because capex and commitments are not netted.

reviews.rationale: The revenue-buoying part is supported by analyst estimates for all three clouds, though AWS's share is small. The claim that the labs cannot exist without tens of billions a year is not established: there is no cash-needs analysis, OpenAI's Q2 data is missing, and Anthropic's positive operating cash flow cuts against it. The compound claim stays open.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion. 'I'd argue' marks it as his position, not a hedge on likelihood.

semantics.note: The present-tense claim that most hyperscaler capex serves OpenAI and Anthropic is preserved. 'Their' refers to Amazon, Microsoft and Google.

contract.note: Reading 'their capex' as total capex, 'vast majority' as well above half, and using Q2 2026 is an ordinary, fair reading.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own disclosure of $41B in quarterly capex, with no allocation by customer. It gives part of the total but not the labs' share.
Anthropic's own announcement of dedicated AWS capacity and commitments. It does not measure what share of Amazon's capex serves Anthropic.

reviews.rationale: No item in the packet allocates any provider's total capex to OpenAI or Anthropic. Total spending figures and announcements of dedicated projects cannot show whether the labs account for most of it, so the claim cannot be settled.
